symptom: At second 12 (Scene 2A), the protagonist's (Alice) head rotated 180 degrees unnaturally while her body remained rear-facing or fixed, morphing facial features directly onto the back of the skull.
root_cause: MiniMax H3 is a 2D diffusion flow-matching video generator lacking 3D skeletal rigging or cel turnaround comprehension. When prompted to transition from walking away into the zoo (rear view) to facing forward and looking at a bird within a continuous take, the model interpolates latents by blending face textures onto the back of the skull rather than executing a physically plausible head/torso turn.
fix_or_workaround: Never force a continuous 180-degree turnaround in a single generative shot. Apply standard animation grammar (a cinematic cut): transition from the rear entrance shot (Scene 1B) to a 3/4 frontal tableau (Scene 2A) where the family is already standing near the willow tree looking upward. The diffusion model then only performs subtle upward gaze, pointing gestures, and arm elevation.

limitations: Requires staging an initial 3/4 tableau keyframe for Scene 2A instead of carrying the raw rear-view frame 119 directly across an axis reversal.
prevention: Rule: If a scene transitions from moving away (rear view) to stationary interaction (front/side view), cut to a new tableau setup rather than forcing continuous rotation.
